title: The module form of the classical equivalence
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a discrete commutative ring, $\Lambda_{X,\Et}$ its constant
sheaf on $X_{\Et}$, and identify $\Lambda_X=\nu_X^*\Lambda_{X,\Et}$. Then
$\nu_X^*$ and $\nu_{X,*}$ restrict to an adjoint pair between
$\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\Mod(X_{\Proet},\Lambda_X)$; the functor
$\nu_X^*\colon\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Proet},\Lambda_X)$ is exact and
fully faithful, and it is an equivalence onto the full subcategory of
classical $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves, with quasi-inverse $\nu_{X,*}$.

proof.text: Write $L=\nu_X^*$ and $R=\nu_{X,*}$ for the set-sheaf adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Its left adjoint preserves finite limits and its right adjoint is restriction; both preserve finite products. Apply $L$ to the addition, zero, negation and action $\Lambda_{X,\Et}\times M\to M$ of a module sheaf ([def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]). Under the product identifications these maps satisfy the module identities because those identities are equalities of maps and $L$ is a functor. This constructs an $L\Lambda_{X,\Et}=\Lambda_X$-module $LM$ and carries linear maps to linear maps. Restriction similarly makes $RG$ an $R\Lambda_X$-module; restrict scalars along $\eta_{\Lambda_{X,\Et}}:\Lambda_{X,\Et}\to R\Lambda_X$. This ring map is an isomorphism by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-unit], and is a ring map since its naturality with addition, multiplication, zero and one gives the corresponding compatibility equations. Naturality with the projections identifies $\eta_{A\times B}$ with $\eta_A\times\eta_B$ and $\varepsilon_{G\times H}$ with $\varepsilon_G\times\varepsilon_H$ under product identifications. Naturality with every module structure map therefore makes $\eta_M$ and $\varepsilon_G$ additive and linear, using the triangle identity $\varepsilon_{L\Lambda_{X,\Et}}\circ L\eta_{\Lambda_{X,\Et}}=1$ for the coefficients of the counit. The usual mutually inverse adjunct maps $a\mapsto R(a)\circ\eta_M$ and $b\mapsto\varepsilon_G\circ L(b)$ consequently carry linear maps to linear maps. Their inverse and naturality identities are those of the set-sheaf adjunction. Thus they define the asserted module adjunction for arbitrary discrete $\Lambda$, without using the finite-ring assertion of the comparison-definition node.

source.place: paragraph 1; explicit product/naturality verification of the module adjunction

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact] to the comparison morphism of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], using the same larger-universe small skeletons as the sites. The underlying abelian inverse image is exact for this morphism of sites; the transported addition in step 1 is precisely its abelian-group structure. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], forgetting a module structure preserves kernels and cokernels, which are respectively sectionwise kernels and sheafified sectionwise cokernels. Accordingly the abelian comparisons $L(\ker f)\cong\ker(Lf)$ and $L(\operatorname{coker}f)\cong\operatorname{coker}(Lf)$ are linear: their maps are induced by the linear kernel inclusion and cokernel quotient, and their inverses are linear because the maps are bijective locally. Thus the module inverse image preserves kernels and cokernels, and is additive by the transported addition. It is exact. This argument needs no finiteness assumption on $\Lambda$; the finite-coefficient node in the imported proof did not itself justify this conclusion.

source.place: paragraph 2, with the finite-coefficient citation replaced by generic exactness; Stacks Tags 04JC and 03DA

proof.text: For module sheaves $M,M'$, [det-pe-classical-sheaves-unit] gives a unique underlying set-sheaf map $\varphi:M\to M'$ lifting each set-sheaf map $h:LM\to LM'$. If $h$ is linear, the equations $\varphi\circ+_M=+_{M'}\circ(\varphi\times\varphi)$, $\varphi\circ0_M=0_{M'}$ and $\varphi\circ a_M=a_{M'}\circ(1_{\Lambda_{X,\Et}}\times\varphi)$ become true after applying $L$, by the product and action identifications in step 1. Faithfulness on all set-sheaf Hom sets, including those with domain $M\times M$, the terminal sheaf and $\Lambda_{X,\Et}\times M$, reflects each of these equalities. Hence $\varphi$ is additive and linear in the sense of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Conversely $L$ sends linear maps to linear maps by step 1. The bijection of underlying Hom sets therefore restricts to a bijection of module Hom sets: $L$ is fully faithful on module sheaves.

source.place: paragraph 3; addition and zero included in the reflection of linearity

proof.text: For the continuity maps of [det-pe-classical-definition-continuity-map], a filtered colimit of $\Lambda$-modules has the same underlying set as the filtered colimit of their sets: represent an element by $[i,x]$, put two representatives at a common later index to add them, and put $r[i,x]=[i,rx]$. Equality means equality after mapping to some common later index, so these operations are well defined and give precisely the module-colimit universal property. Every restriction is linear, so the resulting continuity map is the set continuity map with these operations. A bijective linear map has a linear inverse: if $y=c(x)$ and $y'=c(x')$, then $c^{-1}(y+y')=x+x'$ and $c^{-1}(ry)=rx$. Thus a module sheaf is classical if and only if its underlying set sheaf is classical.

source.place: paragraph 4, first sentence; elementary representative computation supplying the omitted module/set comparison

proof.text: By [det-pe-classical-sheaves-image], the underlying set sheaf of $LM$ is classical, and for any classical underlying set sheaf $G$ its counit $LRG\to G$ is an isomorphism. Step 4 converts both statements to classicality of module sheaves. Step 1 has shown that this counit is linear, hence its inverse is linear by the same calculation as in step 4, applied on sections. The unit is also linear and is an isomorphism on underlying sheaves by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-unit], hence is an isomorphism of modules. Therefore $L$ takes values in the full subcategory of classical module sheaves and its restriction and $R$ have the displayed unit and counit as natural isomorphisms. Their triangle identities are unchanged from step 1. They are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences, with the exactness and full faithfulness proved in steps 2 and 3.

source.place: paragraph 4, remaining sentences; linearity and the actual unit/counit identify the quasi-inverse

split_report.summary: Five steps implement the four blueprint paragraphs: explicit transport of module structures and the adjunction, arbitrary-coefficient exactness, full faithfulness including addition and zero, the elementary module/set filtered-colimit comparison, and the linear unit/counit equivalence. Reused existing nodes only. The finite-coefficient theorem cannot be applied to arbitrary discrete rings, so exactness uses the generic abelian site theorem and the existing module-forgetful kernel/cokernel theorem.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1, 2 and 3 realize paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of the module proof; steps 4 and 5 supply paragraph 4. This is the module clause in the last sentence of the recognizing-classical-part unit proof. No unit or chapter route is replaced.

tool_uses.why: Generic exactness of abelian inverse image is needed in paragraph 2 for arbitrary discrete coefficients; the unit's finite-ring comparison theorem does not cover those coefficients.

Generic preservation of kernels and cokernels by the module-to-abelian forgetful functor converts abelian exactness into module exactness; the classical-equivalence unit has no such general module theorem.
